articles.title: You Can’t See Anything About Billy Evans’s New Start-up
articles.author: Matt Stieb
articles.content:
There’s a lot of exposure for Elizabeth Holmes’s partner in the hit documentary by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, You Can See Everything. Over nearly three hours, you see Billy Evans as a domineering partner and stealth social-media surrogate — and get a glimpse of him fully naked brushing his teeth in the shower. But what the audience doesn’t get, beyond a few glimpses of Holmes and Evans pitching investors on a post-Theranos prototype, is a look at what Evans is working on while Holmes is in prison for running Silicon Valley’s most infamous fraud.
In 2022, five years after he first met Holmes, Evans founded a company called Haemanthus, which is named after a genus of blood lily. Like Theranos, it is a blood-testing start-up with a prototype machine that looks a whole lot like the Edison — the box that falsely promised to run more than 1,000 instant tests with just a pinprick of blood. Little is known about the private company, unlike Theranos, which attracted endless publicity and famous investors. But Evans’s decision to launch a blood-testing company after meeting Holmes is raising a lot of questions about whether this is a Theranos reboot — and whether his partner is onboard. Below is everything we know about Haemanthus, which, inevitably, includes some You Can See Everything spoilers.
What does Haemanthus do?
Haemanthus is developing a test for urine, saliva, and small blood samples promising “a radically new approach to health testing” that could be “the future of diagnostics,” according to marketing materials obtained by the New York Times last year. In pursuit of this radical future, they have come up with a brilliant trick to avoid Food and Drug Administration oversight: They are testing on animals first under the less strict regulatory framework of the Department of Agriculture. Eventually, the plan, per the marketing materials, is total “human health optimization.”
To analyze nonhuman blood and saliva, Haemanthus uses Raman spectroscopy, a type of laser first developed in the 1960s that can determine early-stage markers of ALS and differentiate between malignant and cancerous tissue. The company also states it uses AI to analyze the data. Like with Theranos, its goal is getting the product into a small, PC-sized box for commercial use — and eventually, make it even smaller. In an investor presentation obtained by the Times, the final product would be a small piece of wearable tech, which the company anticipates would take three years and $70 million to make. The ambition is Theranos-like, but that cost is much lower: Holmes raised nearly $1 billion before she was exposed.
In theory, this is all possible. “Handheld Raman instruments the size of a cell phone are already commercially available,” said Igor Lednev, a chemistry professor at SUNY–Albany working on Raman detection for Alzheimer’s. “We are practically working in the same field, trying to develop similar technology.” Eric Potma, a Haemanthus consultant and chemistry professor at UC Irvine, told Wired that “from an engineering perspective, they have some interesting ideas that are worth exploring.”
Who else is involved?
Haemanthus has been fundraising, beginning with $3.15 million from friends and family in the spring of 2025, according to the investor materials seen by the Times, in addition to another $15 million from San Francisco and Austin investors. But because the company is private, there is little information about who is onboard. NPR reports that the company has around a dozen staffers, including some people who worked with Evans at a previous job developing laser sensors for self-driving vehicles.
Evans has said on his social media that he is working on a “stealth” health start-up. “When you’re in stealth, you’re trying to be in stealth,” he told the Times. “They aren’t going to find anything associated with the name Haemanthus.”
The company has also applied for a patent to use AI sensors to run and analyze its tests. The researchers involved in the patent did not respond to requests for comment. The only investor who has publicly come forward is Street Global Venture Capital, a small San Francisco–based firm funding tech start-ups. That firm also did not respond to requests for comment.
What has Haemanthus said?
In a May 2025 post on X, when the Times broke the news of his fundraising efforts, the company stated:
“We’re Haemanthus. Yes, our CEO, Billy Evans, is Elizabeth Holmes’ partner. Skepticism is rational. We must clear a higher bar. When @nytimes contacted us, we invited them: see our lab, tech, and team. They declined. The headline was already written. Our reality inconvenient.”
In a seven-post thread, the account said that the company prefers to “build first, talk later” and that its research will “stand on its own merits.” It added that Haemanthus is “making lab technology accessible through modern lasers and AI.”
As for the animal-research angle, the thread said Haemanthus is starting with veterinary testing “not because it’s easier, but because it’s practical and meaningful.” The thread also stated that it “helps animals who can’t describe symptoms.”
What did Evans do before Haemanthus?
Evans comes from a wealthy California family: His grandparents founded a small chain of luxury hotels that employs over 1,000 people. In a statement before the movie’s release, the company asserted that Evans is not a shareholder or employee.
Evans, 34, attended a private high school in San Diego — tuition today is $49,100 — before graduating from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2015 with a bachelor’s in economics. After college, Evans reportedly tried to create a concierge-medical-service start-up connecting wealthy clients in China with medical care in the United States, setting them up with a chauffeur and luxury hotel stays. “Then he realized that it’s actually very hard to get in with the affluent Chinese community if you’re not fluent in Chinese, so he dropped that,” a source close to Evans told the New York Post in 2019. He worked for LinkedIn for two years before going to work for Luminar, an automated driving company.
Through a representative, Evans declined to comment.
And what about Holmes?
In the Haemanthus thread on X, the company said, “Elizabeth Holmes has zero involvement” and “this is not Theranos 2.0.” Last year, NPR reported that Holmes is listed as a scientific adviser, which the company denied on X.
In the doc, before she reports to prison, Evans and Holmes are discussing a project featuring lasers and AI that Evans describes as “2.0” and an opportunity to “put the band back together and do it all again.” Holmes responds, “From wherever I am, I’m going to continue to work inventing, even if it’s inventing from a cage.” But according to a source close to Evans, the couple was not referring to Haemanthus in this particular conversation but rather an attempt to create a “chemistry-less” system to make testing affordable. When the project resulted in a testing panel that still cost several hundred dollars, it was shelved.
While the company has been clear in its statements that Holmes is not involved, the doc raises some questions as to how Evans is using her likeness. He claims that he has power of attorney over her and that he will post on her social-media accounts without her approval. “It’s a lot easier to make it seem like Elizabeth Holmes is El Chapo running a diagnostics cartel from prison than it is to say, ‘Billy’s building a nerdy company,’” he said on the All-In podcast in October.
articles.summary:
Billy Evans, the partner of Elizabeth Holmes, has launched a secretive blood-testing startup called Haemanthus that utilizes laser technology and AI to pursue radical health diagnostics.

### Key Points
- Haemanthus is developing a diagnostic device that uses Raman spectroscopy to analyze blood, saliva, and urine samples for human health optimization.
- The company is currently bypassing FDA oversight by conducting initial testing on animals under Department of Agriculture regulations.
- Evans has raised approximately $18.15 million in funding, including $3.15 million from friends and family and $15 million from institutional investors.
- The startup aims to shrink its diagnostic technology into a wearable device, projecting a three-year development timeline and a $70 million budget.
- Despite public speculation linking the venture to Theranos, Haemanthus maintains that Elizabeth Holmes has no formal involvement in the company.

### Why it Matters
The launch of Haemanthus invites intense scrutiny due to the founder's personal connection to Elizabeth Holmes and the striking similarities between his startup's goals and the failed Theranos model. Investors and regulators remain cautious, as the company attempts to navigate the high-stakes diagnostics market while managing the reputational baggage associated with the infamous blood-testing fraud.

articles.title: Samsung and SK Hynix are upgrading their NAND factories in China
articles.author: Peter
articles.content:
Chinese memory maker YMTC became China’s biggest producer of NAND flash chips this year with a market share of 38.5%, up from 28% last year. This allowed it to overtake Samsung, which is #2 with 33.5% share (down from 36%) and SK Hynix, which is #3 with 17% (down from 20%). So, now the two Korean companies are working on upgrading their production capacity in China.
Samsung’s facility in Xian, China, accounts for around 40% of its global NAND production capacity. However, it only makes relatively old chips with around 200 layers (more layers = more storage per chip).
There is an ongoing project to upgrade the facility to make NAND V9 chips with 286 layers, writes Reuters. This will start slowly with a planned output of 5,000 wafers by the end of this year and then ramp up massively to 40,000 wafers by the end of 2027.
Samsung NAND production timeline up to v9
V9 is previous generation technology, however. Earlier this year Samsung unveiled NAND V10 with more than 400 layers. V10 has other improvements over V9, including higher speeds and better power efficiency.
Samsung NAND V10 upgrades over V9
SK Hynix has a plant in Dalian, China – this plant was formerly owned by Intel before it was spun off and sold under the name Solidigm. Solidigm has plans to be listed on NASDAQ, but it faces pushback from shareholders and regulators.
Speaking of regulators, companies that want to install US-made semiconductor equipment in China need a license from the Bureau of Industry and Security, which is part of the US Commerce Department. In 2025, the Bureau said that it will not issue licenses to expand or upgrade factories in China, which are owned by foreign chip makers.
Anyway, SK Hynix’s plant in Dalian currently produces 192-layer chips, but insiders say that the company has received the go-ahead from US authorities to upgrade to 240-layer chips and has plans to work on 300+ layer chips, if granted permission. SK Hynix is also in talks about setting up NAND production in the US (with Intel's help), which may help tip the scales.
So when will editors add the part where the first 2 had to defy US sanctions and are now forced to upgrade their Chinese factories to avoid their DDR ram business going the same way with their TV? xD
Translation to Reality: purging more A.I. hardware more and drain consumers wallets flat. The Library is a very nice place. The Gym is a very nice place. The Restaurant is a very nice place. The Garden is a very nice place.
articles.summary:
Chinese memory manufacturer YMTC has overtaken Samsung and SK Hynix to become the leading producer of NAND flash chips in China, prompting the Korean firms to upgrade facilities.

### Key Points
- YMTC captured 38.5% of the Chinese NAND market this year, surpassing Samsung at 33.5% and SK Hynix at 17%.
- Samsung plans to upgrade its Xian facility to produce 286-layer V9 NAND chips, targeting 40,000 wafers per month by 2027.
- SK Hynix received US authorization to upgrade its Dalian plant from 192-layer to 240-layer chip production.
- The US Bureau of Industry and Security plans to restrict licenses for expanding or upgrading foreign-owned semiconductor factories in China starting in 2025.
- SK Hynix is currently exploring potential NAND production partnerships in the United States to diversify its manufacturing footprint.

### Why it Matters
These production shifts highlight the intense competition in the global memory market as companies navigate tightening US export controls on semiconductor technology. The race to increase layer counts and storage density remains critical for maintaining market share against rising domestic Chinese manufacturers.

articles.title: Oppo's Find X10 Pro Max goes all out with three 200MP cameras and a massive battery
articles.author: sanujb6@gmail.com (Sanuj Bhatia) , Sanuj Bhatia
articles.content:
What you need to know
- Oppo has launched the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max, with the latter featuring three 200MP rear cameras for the first time.
- The Find X10 Pro Max features Oppo's new LUMO True Image Engine, alongside 8K video and Open Gate Capture support.
- Both phones pack massive 8,000mAh batteries with 80W wired charging, 50W wireless charging, and 144Hz displays.
- The Find X10 Pro Max uses MediaTek's Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset, while the base Find X10 gets the Dimensity 9600M.
Oppo today officially announced the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max, its latest flagship smartphones for 2026.
The smartphone market in 2026 has been quite topsy-turvy. While phones like the Galaxy S26 Ultra have introduced innovative features like Privacy Display, overall smartphone sales have reportedly fallen to a 14-year low. But that isn't stopping Oppo from going all out with its latest camera-focused flagships.
The company today unveiled the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max, bringing major upgrades across the cameras, battery, chipset, and overall design.
Now, before you ask, there's no regular Find X10 Pro this year. Oppo has announced just two models, the base Find X10 and the top-tier Find X10 Pro Max, with the latter going directly against the likes of the Galaxy S26 Ultra, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and iPhone 18 Pro Max. And the biggest upgrades this year are undoubtedly in the camera department.
As Oppo previously confirmed, the Find X10 Pro Max is the company's first smartphone to feature a triple 200MP camera system. This means you're getting a 200MP main camera, a 200MP ultrawide, and a 200MP telephoto camera on the back. It's an impressive setup, and something we haven't seen on a smartphone before.
But the upgrades don't stop at the camera hardware. Oppo has also introduced its new LUMO True Image Engine, which the company says takes a more natural approach to image processing. According to Oppo, the new engine reproduces colors more accurately across different lighting conditions, whether that's subtle tones in a landscape or more natural-looking skin tones in portraits.
The main camera also uses Samsung's new 1/1.28-inch ISOCELL HPC sensor, which Oppo says it co-developed with Samsung. The sensor features new DeepPix technology designed to improve HDR performance, particularly in challenging lighting conditions.
Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android
Oppo also claims the Find X10 Pro Max is the first smartphone capable of capturing 26MP photos by default across the entire zoom range from 0.5x to 9.9x. We'll be taking a closer look at the camera performance in a separate piece, but on paper, this is shaping up to be one of the most ambitious camera systems we've seen this year.
Video recording is getting plenty of attention too. Oppo says the Find X10 Pro Max can record up to 4K at 60fps, 4K at 120fps, and even 8K at 30fps using its camera system.
For more advanced video workflows, the Find X10 series also supports Dolby Vision, ACES-certified O-Log2, and, for the first time on an Oppo smartphone, Open Gate Capture. Oppo is also working with Blackmagic Camera to bring support for the Find X10 series' camera capabilities to the app.
Coming to the design, both phones retain a similar overall look to last year's Find X9 series, although Oppo has extended the camera module horizontally this time around.
On the front, the base Find X10 features a 6.59-inch display, while the Find X10 Pro Max comes with a larger 6.78-inch panel. Both displays support up to a 144Hz refresh rate and can reach a whopping 3,600 nits of peak brightness.
Oppo has also made some big upgrades to the battery. Both the Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max pack massive 8,000mAh batteries, with support for up to 80W wired charging and 50W wireless charging.
Under the hood, the Find X10 Pro Max is powered by MediaTek's latest Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset, while the base Find X10 uses the 3nm Dimensity 9600M. Both are part of MediaTek's latest flagship chipset family, although the Pro Max gets the more powerful variant.
In terms of the pricing, the Oppo Find X10 starts at €1,399 for the base variant with 256GB of onboard storage and 12GB RAM, whereas the Find 10 Pro Max is available for €1,799. The Find X10 Pro Max comes in a single variant with 12GB RAM and 512GB of onboard storage.
Sanuj is a tech writer who loves exploring smartphones, tablets, and wearables. He began his journey with a Nokia Lumia and later dived deep into Android and iPhone. He's been writing about tech since 2018, with bylines at Pocketnow, Android Police, Pocket-Lint, and MakeUseOf. When he's not testing gadgets, he's either sipping chai, watching football, or playing cricket.

articles.title: Azoma wants to help brands win the AI shopping race. See the pitch deck that helped it raise $11.2 million.
articles.author: Lara O'Reilly
articles.content:
As people begin to delegate online purchases to AI assistants and agents, the startup Azoma wants to ensure its consumer-goods clients make the shopping list.
Azoma works with brands to help their products be discovered by AI shopping agents and platforms, including OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, Alexa for Shopping, and Walmart's Sparky.
The company exclusively told CMO Insider on Wednesday that it had raised an $11.2 million Series A funding round, led by Puma Growth Partners.
Founded in 2022, Azoma initially focused on helping brands show up prominently in AI search and chatbots, operating in the fast-growing field of generative engine optimization, or GEO. Then, over the past year, at least a dozen new AI shopping assistants from retailers rolled out, alongside the launch of personal AI assistants like Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots, and Instinct, which can also make purchases on a user's behalf.
In December, Morgan Stanley estimated that AI-powered shopping assistants could account for up to $385 billion in US e-commerce sales by 2030.
"The space has evolved rapidly from customers just really caring about answer engines to caring about the other types as well," Azoma CEO Max Sinclair told CMO Insider.
Azoma's customers include Unilever, L'Oréal, Reckitt, and Mars. It offers them a service it calls agentic commerce optimization, a technique that helps make their products more discoverable by large language models and more likely to be recommended by them.
Azoma suggests actions the clients can take to improve their visibility, from honing their marketplace listings to optimizing their content on YouTube and Reddit. It also uses "digital twin" technology to simulate different consumer demographics, so brands can see how their products are presented to the specific shoppers they want to target.
Sinclair said Azoma differs from other GEO companies because it's laser-focused on the commerce space and working with brands who sell physical goods.
"Many of our customers have tried these generic GEO platforms and found that they don't understand commerce at all," Sinclair said. "They don't understand the integrations, they don't understand the workflows, they don't understand the existing tech stack, they don't understand how the teams work, how they're operated, how they're motivated."
Sinclair said Azoma plans to invest the fresh funds in ensuring its technology can track across all the latest agents, from Meta's Muse to TikTok's new Shopping Assistant. The company charges a fee per brand, geography, and shopping agent.
Sinclair estimated the company's head count would grow to around 80 to 100 people next year, up from 40 currently, as it ramps up hiring in areas including sales, customer success, AI research, software development, and operations.
Azoma also plans to integrate data from the Tesco-owned retail analytics company Dunnhumby to help brands determine whether increasing their share of voice on a platform like ChatGPT translates into a sales lift at brick-and-mortar retailers.
Dunnhumby Ventures also participated in the round, alongside Twinpath, Mars IAF, Rank Ventures, and Ignite Ventures.
Check out the pitch deck Azoma used to secure its $11.2 million Series A investment, shared exclusively with CMO Insider. Some of the slides have been omitted or redacted.

Azoma quotes Harley Finkelstein, Shopify's president.
Finkelstein said on Shopify's August earnings call that traffic and orders coming in from AI channels to Shopify stores had tripled over the past year.
A Shopify blog post, published in May, said AI-referred traffic converted at a 50% higher rate and had an average order value 14% higher than traditional search.
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy has lauded its AI-powered shopping assistant.
Alexa for Shopping was used by more than 350 million Amazon customers over the past 12 months, Jassy said on the company's July earnings call.
Jassy said that US customers who use Alexa for Shopping spent 40% more per order than those who don't.
Walmart has an AI-powered shopping assistant called Sparky.
Walmart CEO John Furner said on the company's August earnings call that the number of customers using Sparky was up 70% year-on-year. Similar to Amazon, Walmart said customers who used Sparky for shopping spent 40% more per order than those who didn't.

AI commerce startup Azoma has secured $11.2 million in Series A funding to help consumer brands optimize their product visibility across emerging generative AI shopping assistants and platforms.

### Key Points
- Azoma raised $11.2 million in a funding round led by Puma Growth Partners, with participation from Dunnhumby Ventures and others.
- The company provides "agentic commerce optimization" to help brands like Unilever, L'Oréal, and Mars appear in results from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Alexa.
- Azoma utilizes "digital twin" technology to simulate how AI agents present products to specific consumer demographics.
- The startup plans to double its headcount to 100 employees and expand its tracking capabilities to include platforms like TikTok’s Shopping Assistant.
- Morgan Stanley projects that AI-powered shopping assistants could influence up to $385 billion in U.S. e-commerce sales by 2030.

### Why it Matters
As consumers increasingly rely on AI agents for product discovery, brands face a shrinking window of opportunity to influence purchasing decisions. Azoma’s technology addresses this shift by ensuring products remain discoverable in a landscape where generative AI is rapidly replacing traditional search engines.

articles.title: Tesla-SpaceX Merger Being Considered
articles.author: BeauHD
articles.content:
Elon Musk says a merger between Tesla and SpaceX is under active consideration, with special committees at both companies evaluating a deal that could combine businesses valued at roughly $3.5 trillion. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said during a call with financial analysts over the quarterly business results of SpaceX on Tuesday. The BBC reports:  While Musk noted the certainty of such a merger should not be assumed, and it would need shareholders' support, he said special committees within both companies have been formed to examine the move. "The special committees have not reached agreement on terms of any transaction and there's no guarantee that they will," Musk added. "But I do think there is a lot of merit to merging and a lot to be gained."
[...] The company, which builds space rockets and Starlink internet satellites, is now expanding into offering cloud compute capacity for other tech companies, like Anthropic and Google. That line of business has become the most profitable part of SpaceX, bringing in $7.5bn according to the latest quarterly results (PDF). Starlink also tallied revenue of $5.2bn. SpaceX as a whole, however, is not profitable and has lost $1.1bn so far this year.
[...] Musk said on Tuesday a full merger between the two companies would make sense for the work each is doing around chips, artificial intelligence, software and more. He described himself as a "conflicted party" as the chief executive of Tesla and of SpaceX. Even commenting on the possibility of a merger between the two companies, Musk compared to "tap dancing through a minefield." He added a merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders. At least 50% of Tesla's shareholders would need to approve the merger, which Musk described as "quite a high hurdle to achieve."
articles.summary:
Elon Musk has confirmed that special committees at Tesla and SpaceX are actively evaluating a potential merger that could combine two companies with a combined $3.5 trillion valuation.

### Key Points
- Elon Musk stated that special committees at both companies are currently examining the feasibility of a potential merger.
- A successful deal would require approval from at least 50% of Tesla shareholders, a threshold Musk described as a significant hurdle.
- SpaceX reported $7.5 billion in revenue from its cloud computing division and $5.2 billion from Starlink, despite an overall year-to-date loss of $1.1 billion.
- Musk cited potential synergies in artificial intelligence, software development, and chip technology as primary motivations for combining the two entities.
- No formal agreement on transaction terms has been reached, and Musk emphasized that there is no guarantee a merger will proceed.

### Why it Matters
A merger between these two industry giants would create a massive, vertically integrated conglomerate spanning automotive, aerospace, and artificial intelligence sectors. This consolidation could fundamentally reshape the tech and energy markets, though it faces significant regulatory scrutiny and shareholder approval challenges.

articles.title: FADU puts the filesystem inside the SSD's flash to bypass host CPUs
articles.author: Shane Downing
articles.content:
SSD controller designer FADU’s new File-Semantic SSD (FS-SSD) was announced at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The new device promises to move the file system into the SSD itself. As detailed in a white paper, this enables GPUs, DPUs, and NICs to open and read files with “no host filesystem, no block layer, and no storage-server CPU in the path.” FADU told Tom’s Hardware Premium it expects partner samples by Q3 2027.
FADU is a Seoul, South Korea-based fabless SSD controller designer. Its FS-SSD technology is designed to handle and improve the control path, as the data path side moved to accelerators years ago. FADU’s measurements show that the file system, plus block layers, can consume about 30% of CPU cycles in a GPUDirect Storage (GDS) random-read workload. It notes that bypass options give up the files, and the company claims its solution promises the best of both worlds.
In FADU’s own preliminary Network File System (NFS) over NVMe test, on a drive built on its FC6161 Gen6 controller in a PCIe 5.0 host, remote file throughput held steady as the server downshifted from what FADU labels 16 cores to just one, maintaining about 460,000 ops/s.
The NFSv3 operations are carried inside standard NVMe commands, and the drive handles path lookup, access control, and file-to-flash mapping. FS-SSD’s performance is remarkable when compared to Linux NFS-over-RDMA, which achieved a third of the ops/s with 16 cores and only 40K ops/s with one core. The technology remains “under active development,” and FADU told Tom’s Hardware Premium it expects Gen6-host results by Q1 2027, with partner samples in Q3 2027.
FADU chooses to use NFSv3 because it’s “small (21 operations), OS- and filesystem-agnostic, and stateless” with low firmware overhead. FS-SSD supports PCIe today, with NVMe-oF over RDMA and TCP working without any new transport needed. Reusing an existing protocol is a smart move, in our view. Under the hood, the file system and flash translation layer are merged with a file layer derived from F2FS. Node and data blocks are aligned with the natural flash pages, sections at corresponding erase units, so that the F2FS node table becomes a “File Map” pointing the node IDs at physical flash addresses.
One big advantage is that the DRAM mapping metadata overhead is considerably smaller: it uses the same amount of DRAM as a standard SSD, ~0.1% of NAND capacity (about 1 GB per TB), which a standard SSD fills almost entirely with its mapping table. Here, most of that DRAM, ~95%, can act as a hot-path node cache.
One garbage collector also replaces two, avoiding what FADU calls the “double GC” of host F2FS, where file-system cleanup and the drive’s own garbage collection amplify each other. Write amplification is also 63% lower versus a host F2FS solution on a mixed sequential and random workload with FADU’s research prototype, the company said. FADU told Tom's Hardware Premium that the prototype runs synthetic fio workloads on NVMeVirt, an open-source software SSD emulator from Seoul National University, so it is not a hardware result.
Most importantly for this method, it ensures host-free access. The GPU builds NFS-over-NVMe commands in queues in its own memory, which could include HBM. Alternatively, a remote SmartNIC or DPU with NVMe-oF target offload can drop commands in the drive’s submission queue. The data goes from SSD to NIC via PCIe peer-to-peer DMA, coming out as RDMA writes. FADU’s explicitly named use cases for this include GPU file reads and checkpoints, DPU-served HTTP content delivery, and a JBoF (just a bunch of flash) file server.
FADU’s numbers for its internal test come from a client and server Intel Core i5-13600K, a CPU with 20 threads that clocks up to 5.1 GHz with 128GB of DDR5, and a Mellanox ConnectX-6 100 Gbps NIC. Synthetic testing is compared using fio with the baseline F2FS and Ext4 on block firmware versus the FS-SSD via a kernel client and an SPDK user-space client. The sequential test is 1 thread, queue depth (QD) 128, with 128KB blocks, while random is at 4 threads, the same QD128, but with 4KB blocks.
These block sizes are typical for client workloads in our experience, so they are a fair measure, with detailed preliminary results in the table below. Against SPDK on the raw drive, figures FADU provided to us, FS-SSD’s SPDK client keeps about 93% on 4K random read and 53% on 4K random write, via fio, with around a 7% and 47% cost for the in-drive file layer. Though the raw drive’s 13,240 MB/s random write is above the ~12 GB/s FADU gives as the NAND’s program bandwidth, those runs likely weren’t at steady state. The Filebench result is particularly interesting, as the SPDK random gains apply to a plain block device too.
This should be the workload most favorable for the technology, as the Filebench file server is metadata-heavy with relatively high host overhead: FADU says it uses 10,000 files in a multi-level tree, mean directory width 20, and a mean file size of 128KB with 50 client threads.
| FADU’s preliminary fio results: Gen6 controller in a PCIe 5.0 host, direct I/O |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Setup | Sequential read (MB/s) | Sequential write (MB/s) | 4KB random read (MB/s) | 4KB random write (MB/s) | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F2FS | 14,120 | 4,510 | 7,850 | 3,980 | 
| Ext4 | 14,130 | 7,050 | 9,120 | 4,560 | 
| FS-SSD (kernel client) | 14,140 | 11,940 | 8,070 | 4,320 | 
| FS-SSD (SPDK client) | Not reported | Not reported | 13,000 | 7,030 | 
| Raw block (SPDK) | Not reported | Not reported | 13,990 | 13,240 | 
One important thing to recall is that although this test is on a Gen6 drive, the test results are on a PCIe 5.0 host. Therefore, every sequential read config tops out at around 14.1 GB/s, which is roughly the link limit. The testbed also uses a consumer-class desktop CPU, while the one-core NFS server is a showcase example. The kernel client ends up 11.5% behind Ext4 on random read and 5.3% behind on random write, again by our math.
One example of a tough question more generally is: how do concurrent GPU, DPU, and host writers coordinate? How does a kernel mount’s page cache stay coherent with GPU access? NFSv3 storage devices, by the pNFS Flexible File Layout spec (RFC 8435), are “always treated as loosely coupled,” which means “Mandatory byte-range locking cannot be supported.”
Credentials riding in the NVMe command may also face security issues, as loosely coupled devices get only “a level of security equivalent to AUTH_SYS,” NFS’s basic scheme, in which the server trusts whatever user and group IDs the client sends. FADU’s published material also does not describe features such as snapshots, encryption handling, quotas, ACLs, crash handling, and so forth, related to this. Statelessness is what makes it work, but it doesn’t solve all problems, so the trust factor moves elsewhere.
In reply to our questioning, FADU said that there is no cross-host locking, as NFS’s lock manager isn’t implemented. The drive applies each write whole, in order. If two writes hit the same spot, the second one wins; this is “last-writer-wins.” Coordination depends on the clients: kernel-mounted ones get the usual advisory locks among themselves, GPU and SPDK clients coordinate in the application, and at scale a pNFS metadata server handles the coordination. Caching is also handled like ordinary NFS, with kernel clients, or is not done at all, for GPU and SPDK clients. This is stock NFSv3 behavior.
The drive has to check user/group IDs against the file permissions itself. Because those IDs ride inside the command, a client could fake them, but FADU says it closes that issue with capability-based authentication. Each command carries a capability issued by an outside authentication server, plus a code computed with a key shared only between that server and the drive. This is not detailed in its published material. FADU adds that support for the Kerberos authentication protocol is planned. For networked drives, the standard NVMe-oF protections are used, with only pre-approved hosts admitted. A drive trusts a single host’s kernel like any NVMe drive.
However, as FADU described to us, ACLs and other features are missing in the current release, aside from encryption, which in this case is handled by the FC6161’s standard TCG Opal self-encrypting drive support. Power loss is also typically handled with capacitors flushing metadata, the write buffer, and a log of in-flight operations. On restart, the drive replays the unfinished operations, and every write is durable if the drive acknowledges it.
FADU’s longer sights are on producing a JBoF storage solution with no server in front: FS-SSDs, a PCIe switch, and a DPU or NIC for handling NVMe-oF in hardware. FADU’s model puts this at about 42% lower power, about 57% lower cost per 16-drive server, and higher rack density with significantly lower five-year total cost of ownership. The drives would slot in behind existing pNFS metadata servers and could scale. FADU’s controllers already ship with drives such as the SN861, which Western Digital launched and SanDisk now sells, but this would expand the options and solutions it can provide.
| FADU’s FS-SSD roadmap |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Milestone | Timing (per FADU) | Details | 
|---|---|---|
| Gen6-host results | By Q1 2027 | FS-SSD tested in a PCIe 6.0 host; hardware write-amplification figures to come with them | 
| Partner samples | Q3 2027 | OEM/ODM talks are at an early stage; active collaboration expected once samples ship | 
| Hostless JBoF | By end of 2027 | Reference design built on Xsight Labs E1 DPUs, delivered to OEM/ODM partners | 
| GPU access | Now, via GPUDirect Storage | Works with GDS through the kernel client; FADU intends to join the Accelerated IO SIG (xio-sig), where Nvidia open-sourced cuFile; no direct engagement with Nvidia | 
| Standards | Nothing submitted yet | FADU plans to start a file-semantic command set discussion at NVM Express and OCP Storage; samples and client code come first | 
Next year should bring real numbers and samples, with the JBoF reference design also expected. There may be an NVM Express or OCP Storage proposal down the line for a file-semantic command set to further cement and mature the approach. FADU has a good idea, is building it on an existing framework, and has a testbed with results and a hardware path forward on its Gen6 controller, with a trust model in mind. A Gen6-host run is now needed to support the company’s claims.
articles.summary:
FADU has unveiled its File-Semantic SSD (FS-SSD) technology, which integrates file system operations directly into the drive to enable host-free data access for GPUs and accelerators.

### Key Points
- The FS-SSD architecture offloads file system, block layer, and CPU tasks to the drive, potentially reducing CPU cycle consumption by 30%.
- FADU utilizes the NFSv3 protocol to handle path lookups, access control, and file-to-flash mapping within standard NVMe commands.
- Preliminary testing shows the technology maintains high throughput even when server resources are significantly reduced, outperforming traditional Linux NFS-over-RDMA.
- The design reduces write amplification by 63% by eliminating the "double garbage collection" conflict between host file systems and SSD firmware.
- FADU expects to provide partner samples by Q3 2027, with a hostless JBoF reference design planned for the end of 2027.

### Why it Matters
By moving file management directly onto the storage controller, this technology could significantly lower latency and power consumption for data-intensive AI and high-performance computing workloads. This approach allows GPUs and DPUs to access data without relying on a traditional host CPU, potentially reshaping the efficiency and cost structure of large-scale storage infrastructure.

articles.title: Optable’s Agentic Marketplace Bets That AI Agents Can Return More Dollars To Working Media
articles.author: AdExchanger Content Studio
articles.content:
Programmatic advertising made media buying scalable but at a cost: Standardized impression auctions often obscure a publishers’ unique value, while a complex supply chain eats up nearly half of advertising spend.
Now, agentic AI promises something better: the speed and scale of programmatic combined with the customization and direct relationships of traditional media buying. And cutting out unnecessary intermediary fees is the cherry on top.
That’s the vision behind Optable’s new Agentic Marketplace, unveiled October 8 at Optable Connect 2026 in New York City. The platform connects buyer and seller AI agents, and their data, to automate the discovery, packaging and purchasing of publisher inventory.
“Programmatic solved the problem of scaling transactions, but in the process, we lost much of the context and collaboration that made direct advertising valuable,” said Bosko Milekic, Optable’s co-founder and chief product officer. “Agentic AI gives us an opportunity to scale those one-to-one conversations – and fundamentally rethink how advertising is bought and sold.”
Bringing buyers and sellers together – at scale and speed
Direct advertising deals traditionally require extensive back-and-forth between agency planners, publisher sales teams and ad operations staff to identify inventory, build audience packages, negotiate terms and execute orders. That manual work makes customized deals difficult to scale for publishers – and economically impractical for many advertisers.
Optable wants AI agents to automate the publisher-to-buyer conversations – preserving the customization of direct deals without the manual work that has historically limited their reach.
In the Agentic Marketplace, publishers package inventory, audience data, targeting options and pricing into advertising products that buyer agents can discover. Those agents interpret campaign briefs, connect to advertiser data and identify relevant offerings.
Buyers connect their own agents through a single integration, and those agents can then assemble media plans and submit orders directly to publishers, who retain control over pricing, buyer eligibility and deal approvals. Approved orders flow into existing ad servers for review and execution.
At Connect, Paul Frampton-Calero, CEO of independent media agency Goodway Group, described how agentic technology accelerated campaign execution: “We basically built the whole briefing, prompted it, and it went all the way through to the buying agent. The whole thing was taken from start to QA in the space of, I think, 30 minutes.”
The marketplace also gives publishers visibility into buyer demand, including briefs that don’t match their existing advertising products. Those insights could inform new offerings based on actual advertiser demand.
“It’s not about just throwing your inventory against the wall anymore,” said Amanda Martin, chief revenue officer at Mediavine, during a panel at Optable Connect. “It’s about merchandising your inventory and presenting it in different ways so that buyers can choose what they want.”
Making direct advertising accessible to more buyers and sellers
By automating dealmaking, agentic AI could radically expand which products get sold, which publishers can sell them and which advertisers can afford to buy them.
Premium sponsorships, homepage takeovers, custom audience packages and other products that don’t fit neatly into conventional programmatic workflows could become available for automated, on-demand purchase by buyer agents — without weeks of negotiation or setup.
This technology won’t eliminate the need for human judgment and relationships. Optable’s VP of Product, Andy Sharkey, highlighted that publishers will still need to articulate what makes their audiences valuable, establish pricing strategies and build trust with buyers.
But smaller publishers could reach more advertisers without building large sales and ad ops teams, and larger publishers could scale customized offerings beyond the major buyers that typically justify the manual effort.
It also changes the economics for buyers. With AI agents handling the work of building customized direct campaigns, advertisers could explore more publishers and assemble tailored campaigns without all the admin overhead. This would expand the market for direct advertising, giving advertisers practical access to premium inventory and publisher data no matter the size of their budget or media team.
Rethinking the ad tech tax
Optable is also challenging the economics of advertising transactions: According to eMarketer data presented at Connect, approximately 41% of US real-time bidding digital display spending goes toward programmatic fees in 2026.
By scaling direct transactions, Optable aims to direct more dollars toward working media. To support this goal, the company won’t charge additional transaction or activation fees to Optable customers who contract and invoice each other directly. The Agentic Marketplace offers a separate paid option for buyers that want advanced targeting and measurement as well as centralized transaction clearing across publishers. But, critically, that cost is paid as a service instead of a per-transaction fee – and, either way, publishers pay nothing to sell through the marketplace.
Optable leaders framed this as a shift in incentives: Ad tech should be compensated for its technology rather than automatically collecting a percentage of advertising spend. “Software should be paid for as software,” said Optable Co-Founder and CEO Vlad Stesin during his opening remarks at Optable Connect.
Stesin and other Optable leaders made it clear that disintermediation is not the goal, noting that DSPs, SSPs and other providers offer valuable services, including measurement, verification, targeting and optimization. But direct agent-to-agent transactions could let buyers decide which services they need and which fees are justified.
Moreover, Optable’s Milekic warned that agentic advertising could still evolve down a different path: If every intermediary introduces its own agent – and continues collecting a percentage of media spend – agentic advertising could recreate today’s complexity and inefficiencies at machine speed.
Proving the business case
For now, agentic advertising remains a tiny market. Emarketer projections shared at Connect put agentic media buying at $100 million in 2026, potentially growing to $3.9 billion in 2027 and $29.5 billion in 2028.
“There’s a lot of audience discovery happening, but not as much transaction,” said Dave Lundell, vice president of product development at Hearst, during a publisher panel.
That gap highlights a familiar tech adoption paradox: Both sides need a business case before committing significant resources, but each depends on the other’s participation to prove the model works.
Buyers and agencies need evidence that agentic buying delivers better campaign outcomes – an advantage they can use to win and retain advertisers. Publishers need confidence that incremental revenue will justify investments in organizing audience data and adapting their infrastructure to support automated transactions.
Of course, Milekic’s warning still looms: Whether the industry uses the capabilities of agentic AI to simplify advertising transactions – or merely adds another layer to the existing supply chain – remains to be seen.
For Optable, the new marketplace represents a bet that the industry is ready for more than faster transactions. It’s a new model of media buying that preserves programmatic scale and data-driven buying while addressing the friction, complexity and unnecessary costs of the status quo.

### Key Points

- Optable aims to reduce the "ad tech tax," noting that approximately 41% of U.S. real-time bidding display spending currently goes toward intermediary fees.

By prioritizing software-based service fees over percentage-based transaction taxes, the model could significantly increase the portion of advertising budgets that reach actual working media.

articles.title: Live updates: Bitcoin clings to $82,500 as SpaceX results lift stock futures
articles.author: Shaurya Malwa
articles.content:
Bitcoin is hanging just above $82,500 on Wednesday, the level XS.com’s Simon-Peter Massabni calls its most important support, as stock futures climbed on SpaceX’s blowout results and oil pushed back above $110.
Bitcoin’s fate is tied to tech again. It fell in lockstep with the Nasdaq last week after the hot U.S. inflation report and a selloff in AI and chip stocks, and Massabni, XS.com’s head of business development, said that link is getting stronger.
“In the short term, this development challenges the notion that Bitcoin can consistently serve as an independent safe haven from traditional market volatility,” he said.
A “decisive and sustained break” below $82,500 could hand control to sellers and expose bitcoin to a drop toward $70,000, Massabni said. That’s the downside case laid out by market maker Wintermute, and it would mean a further 15% slide from here.
Tech gave bitcoin some cover on Wednesday. 
Nasdaq 100 futures rose 0.4% and S&P 500 futures 0.2%. SpaceX jumped 9% before the open after its AI and satellite internet businesses drove earnings well above forecasts, and a report that Anthropic may spend $750 billion on computing power eased worries about the AI spending boom. 
Brent topped $110 a barrel on attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, and Treasury yields edged higher. Meta and Tesla report later Wednesday.
A move back above $84,000 would take the $70,000 scenario off the table.
articles.summary:
Bitcoin remains precariously positioned above the critical $82,500 support level as the cryptocurrency’s price continues to track closely with broader volatility in the technology sector and stock markets.

### Key Points
- Bitcoin is currently trading just above $82,500, a threshold analysts identify as a vital support level to prevent a potential slide toward $70,000.
- Market maker Wintermute warns that a sustained break below the current support could trigger a 15% decline in the asset's value.
- SpaceX shares rose 9% in pre-market trading following strong earnings results from its artificial intelligence and satellite internet divisions.
- Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 0.4% as reports of significant computing power investments by Anthropic helped stabilize investor sentiment regarding the AI sector.
- Brent crude oil prices surpassed $110 per barrel following reports of regional attacks near the Strait of Hormuz.

### Why it Matters
The strengthening correlation between Bitcoin and tech stocks challenges the narrative that the cryptocurrency functions as an independent safe haven during periods of market instability. Investors are closely monitoring these price levels to determine if Bitcoin will maintain its current valuation or face a deeper correction tied to broader macroeconomic trends.

articles.title: I installed this Linux distro for gaming and stayed for something else
articles.author: Dipan Saha
articles.content:
When it comes to performance-focused Linux distributions, there are quite a few to speak of. All of these seem to be based on either Arch or Fedora in some form or the other, functioning (mostly) the same. Like many of you, I’ve been using Bazzite for quite some time now, but its immutable file system presented a few challenges. There aren't a lot of things you can tweak or modify, and some of the defaults aren’t to my liking.
Which is where CachyOS comes into play again. This is a highly optimized version of Arch Linux, making it ideal for resource-intensive workloads like gaming. Curious, I took it out for a spin on my server and ended up switching to it on one of my spare laptops. It's been there ever since.
CachyOS isn’t immutable, and that’s one of its biggest draws
It also happens to be based on Arch Linux
Bazzite is an immutable operating system. In other words, you cannot make changes to certain core sections of the operating system, at least not as easily. This makes persistent changes a lot more difficult to implement.
Moreover, it’s just not how I like my operating systems to be built. I prefer having total control and a full layout of the whole installation architecture, so that I can know exactly what to pinpoint to when something goes awry. Which is why I have gravitated toward Arch Linux after spending months distro hopping.
Despite this, vanilla Arch Linux is just a pain to set up whether you use the Archinstall script or not. This is where Arch-derivatives like CachyOS turn out to be saviors. They offer an easy, pre-configured Calamares installer that makes the worst part of Arch a breeze.
For my particular use case, it was a Proxmox server with a RX 9070 passed through into a SteamOS-like installation. This was so I could boot into a gaming system whenever I needed, and access it across the network.
Bazzite worked, but there weren’t many things I could change, and so the next option was CachyOS. Being based on Arch Linux unlocks access to the Arch User Repository or AUR, a collection of installer scripts that house almost every program you could think of.
Combine that with CachyOS’s own system-level optimizations, custom-tuned packages and kernels, and you have an incredibly performant, snappy Linux distribution.
Setting CachyOS up for gaming was also incredibly straightforward, requiring the cachyos-gaming-meta package along with Protonplus for the custom Proton versions. This also deploys Steam, and the GPU-specific drivers.
If you're feeling experimental, it’s also possible to install the Steam Machine’s gaming mode user interface onto Cachy for a plug-and-play system.
CachyOS is also a fantastic desktop operating system
KDE Plasma really cements the overall experience
The best way to experience CachyOS (especially if you’re coming from Windows) is to stick to the default KDE Plasma desktop interface during the installation. KDE is fantastic, and one of the best desktop environments for Linux.
It’s also modular, and surprisingly easy to get into. Sure, it might not be as seamless as GNOME, but KDE is miles ahead of alternatives like LXQt and Hyprland in terms of its accessibility.
Circling back to Windows users, KDE just feels like a souped-up version of Windows 11, with all the right tweaks and features. You could even say that it offers a superior experience.
It’s the default for a reason, and still my go-to desktop environment of choice. CachyOS is absolutely phenomenal with KDE, and most things just work, including Nvidia cards. The open-source suite of apps continues to keep growing, and makes it an excellent desktop operating system as my daily driver.
Switching to CachyOS and its packages on a spare laptop
Trying out CachyOS was enough to convince me to make the switch. And so I did, installing it on an older Dell Latitude (the 7320). It’s been a week since, and I see no reason to switch it over to any other Linux distribution.
CachyOS has the familiarity of Arch Linux and the strengths of a source-based operating system like Gentoo, having tailor-made packages for each kind of system architecture. This makes it blazing fast, and the difference in responsiveness is noticeable, especially on weaker hardware.
However, there’s an alternative for those who don’t want to completely give in to the automated defaults of CachyOS. There’s a handy series of helper scripts from the official CachyOS website that lets you convert an existing Arch Linux installation.
The CPU architecture is auto-detected, and the installer replaces the older packages with the appropriate CachyOS package. This also adds in the CachyOS repos (and its kernels), which have a few pre-compiled binaries.
articles.summary:
CachyOS offers a high-performance, Arch-based Linux distribution that provides users with full system control, optimized kernels, and an accessible installation process for gaming and daily desktop use.

### Key Points
- CachyOS is a performance-focused, mutable Linux distribution based on Arch Linux that avoids the restrictions of immutable systems like Bazzite.
- The operating system features a user-friendly Calamares installer, simplifying the complex setup process typically associated with vanilla Arch Linux.
- Users gain access to the Arch User Repository (AUR) and custom-tuned, architecture-specific packages designed to improve system responsiveness.
- Gaming performance is enhanced through the cachyos-gaming-meta package, which integrates Steam, Protonplus, and necessary GPU drivers.
- The distribution defaults to the KDE Plasma desktop environment, offering a familiar, modular interface suitable for users transitioning from Windows.
- Existing Arch Linux installations can be converted to CachyOS using official helper scripts that auto-detect CPU architecture and apply optimized repositories.

### Why it Matters
CachyOS provides a compelling alternative for power users who demand the performance of a source-based system without the manual overhead of traditional Arch Linux. By balancing deep system customization with an accessible installation, it serves as a viable daily driver for both gaming enthusiasts and general desktop users.

articles.title: Critical PHP Core Security Flaws Affect Websites, Including WordPress via @sejournal, @vahandev
articles.author: Vahan Petrosyan
articles.content:
The PHP security team has released emergency fixes today, October 21, 2026, for two critical flaws that can let attackers run code on website servers without logging in.
The fixed versions are PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. PHP says updating is the only safe choice because no workaround fully addresses the vulnerabilities.
PHP says all installations serving website requests are at risk. Apache servers using mod_php, which runs PHP directly inside Apache, face the highest risk. A demonstrated attack can run before the website’s own code starts.
PHP runs WordPress on your web server. Updating WordPress or its plugins will not update PHP. Ask your host to install the fix. If your hosting account lets you switch PHP versions through cPanel, confirm that the version you select includes the patch.
Older PHP Versions Need An Upgrade
PHP 8.1 and older remain on the end-of-life list and no longer receive regular official updates.
For this emergency, PHP has provided limited source-code fixes for PHP 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1 for teams that build PHP themselves. Hosting providers and long-term support vendors may also supply their own updates. These fixes do not restore ongoing support. Ask your host to confirm protection while arranging an upgrade to a supported version.
Government Sites Taken Offline Ahead Of The PHP Patch
International Cyber Digest reported that Dutch parliament and cyber agency websites, Finnish government web services, and university sites went offline ahead of the release. It described the Finnish shutdowns as a precaution, not a breach.
Sansec also reported that the Dutch House of Representatives and National Cyber Security Centre took their websites offline as a precaution.
Ahead of the release, CERT-EU and the UK National Cyber Security Centre advised considering temporary isolation or shutdowns where immediate protection was not possible.
What Website Owners Should Do Now
Follow the WordPress PHP guide to check your version: open Tools > Site Health, select Info, and expand Server.
- Ask your host to install one of the fixed versions listed above, or confirm that its PHP update includes both fixes.
- If you use PHP 8.1 or older, back up the site and arrange an upgrade. Ask your host whether it can apply a vendor-provided fix in the meantime.
If you cannot patch immediately, discuss taking the affected site offline until it can be updated. A web application firewall (WAF), such as Cloudflare, may block some attack attempts, but it is not a substitute for installing the fixes.
If you take your site offline to patch PHP, ask your host to show a maintenance page with an HTTP 503 (Service Unavailable) response, as Google recommends. This signals a temporary outage; your host can serve the page through the web server or a content delivery network (CDN), without relying on PHP.
If you use a firewall, make sure all visits pass through it. Attackers who can reach your website’s server directly can bypass those checks.
After patching, check for web shells (malicious scripts that give attackers access), unfamiliar admin accounts, and unexpected PHP file changes. A patch does not remove an existing compromise.
See also: Google Reminds Sites To Serve A 503 During PHP Patch Downtime
Prepare For More Severe Vulnerabilities
As I predicted in August when writing about how AI is changing website security, attackers can move faster than software makers can deliver a fix. Reports of an attack tool circulating before this PHP patch show that timing problem is already happening.
The fix is now available, but it only protects your site once installed. A compromise can expose customer data and damage search visibility.
Ask your tech team to audit your code and monitor suspicious activity. Agree with your host who will apply emergency patches or take an affected site offline if it cannot be protected.
Attackers can use uncensored models with safety restrictions removed. These models can gain capabilities through distillation, which trains them on outputs from more powerful frontier models. As a result, more powerful AI can reach bad actors without the original models’ safeguards, giving them better tools to find and exploit weaknesses. That is why I expect severe vulnerabilities like these to be uncovered more frequently, with less time for website owners to respond. Preparing for that pace is becoming part of protecting your website and its search visibility.
Featured Image: Popartic/Shutterstock
articles.summary:
The PHP security team released emergency patches on October 21, 2026, to address two critical vulnerabilities that allow unauthorized remote code execution on vulnerable web servers.

### Key Points
- PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 contain the necessary security fixes for these critical flaws.
- Apache servers utilizing mod_php are at the highest risk, as attackers can execute code before the website's own scripts load.
- Website owners must contact their hosting providers to verify or install the updates, as updating WordPress or plugins does not patch the underlying PHP.
- PHP 8.1 and older versions are end-of-life, though limited source-code fixes are available for versions 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1.
- Several government and university websites in the Netherlands and Finland were taken offline as a precautionary measure prior to the patch release.
- Security experts recommend auditing sites for existing compromises, such as web shells, because patching does not remove unauthorized access already gained by attackers.

### Why it Matters
These vulnerabilities pose a severe threat to website integrity and user data, as they allow attackers to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary code. Because exploit tools are already circulating, immediate action is required to prevent potential breaches that could lead to long-term damage to site security and search engine visibility.

articles.title: Your WordPress.com Site is Protected Against the Recent Critical PHP Vulnerabilities
articles.author: Ian Stewart
articles.content:
Today, the PHP project released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution. PHP is the programming language WordPress runs on, which is why it matters to every WordPress site.
If your site is hosted on WordPress.com, there’s nothing you need to do to keep your site safe from these vulnerabilities. 
Your sites are already protected against the recently disclosed PHP security issues. Automattic worked closely with the PHP Security team to ensure that all sites hosted on our platform were protected as soon as possible, ensuring all sites hosted with Automattic, including those on WordPress.com, WordPress VIP, WP Cloud, Pressable, and Tumblr, are safe. If you run your own servers, update now.
Why you didn’t have to lift a finger
On WordPress.com, PHP is installed, maintained, and patched by us at the infrastructure level, not by you. Our security team prepared for this release ahead of time, so every site on the platform is covered.
That’s the difference between doing it yourself and managed hosting (like what you get on WordPress.com). At many hosts, the site owner is responsible for security: updating software, installing a security plugin, watching for threats. On WordPress.com, we handle it for you.
How WordPress.com protects your site every day
This week’s news isn’t one-off work for our team; we ensure that these protections are on all the time for WordPress.com sites:
- Automatic updates: We keep your WordPress version up to date automatically.
- Encryption by default: Every WordPress.com site, including custom domains, is served over SSL, and insecure requests are redirected to HTTPS.
- Daily malware scans: Jetpack Scan checks every WordPress.com site daily for dangerous plugins, themes, and malware. Our security team resolves what it finds, and we email you if we have to remove something.
- A firewall in front of your site: Our web application firewall examines incoming traffic and blocks suspicious IP addresses, malicious bots, and unusual activity.
- Monitoring: We watch for suspicious activity, including brute-force login attempts and DDoS attacks, and alert you if your site goes down.
- Backups: We back up site data regularly, and sites on higher-level plans can access daily backups from the dashboard.
Your part
Of course, security works both ways, and there are still some things that you can do to ensure your site stays secure: use a strong password, turn on two-step authentication, keep your account email current, and review plugins and user roles regularly.
You don’t need to install a separate security plugin, and some can interfere with the protections you already get by using WordPress.com.
No service can promise perfect security, and we won’t pretend otherwise. On WordPress.com, security is our job to solve, not yours.
